changes.before: though at a rate that has been insufficient to bring down unemployment.
changes.after: though at a rate that has been insufficient to bring about a significant improvement in labor market conditions.

changes.before: Household spending is increasing at a moderate pace, but remains constrained
changes.after: Growth in household spending picked up late last year, but remains constrained

changes.before: Business spending on equipment and software is rising, though less rapidly than earlier in the year, while investment in nonresidential structures continues to be weak.
changes.after: Business spending on equipment and software is rising, while investment in nonresidential structures is still weak.

changes.before: Longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable, but measures of underlying inflation have continued to trend downward.
changes.after: Although commodity prices have risen, longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable, and measures of underlying inflation have been trending downward.

changes.before: In addition, the Committee intends to purchase $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities by the end of the second quarter of 2011, a pace of about $75 billion per month.
changes.after: In particular, the Committee is maintaining its existing policy of reinvesting principal payments from its securities holdings and intends to purchase $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities by the end of the second quarter of 2011.

changes.before: Voting against the policy was Thomas M. Hoenig.

parsed.rationale: The economic description is modestly firmer (spending picked up, investment no longer slowing, commodity prices noted), but policy guidance, the asset purchase program and the extended-period language are unchanged. The dissent vanished because of the voter rotation, so the change in tone is minor overall.

spans.quote: though at a rate that has been insufficient to bring down unemployment.
Household spending is increasing at a moderate pace, but remains constrained
Business spending on equipment and software is rising, though less rapidly than earlier in the year, while investment in nonresidential structures continues to be weak.
Longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable, but measures of underlying inflation have continued to trend downward.
In addition, the Committee intends to purchase $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities by the end of the second quarter of 2011, a pace of about $75 billion per month.
Voting against the policy was Thomas M. Hoenig.
though at a rate that has been insufficient to bring about a significant improvement in labor market conditions.
Growth in household spending picked up late last year, but remains constrained
Business spending on equipment and software is rising, while investment in nonresidential structures is still weak.
Although commodity prices have risen, longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable, and measures of underlying inflation have been trending downward.

In particular, the Committee is maintaining its existing policy of reinvesting principal payments from its securities holdings and intends to purchase $600 billion of longer-term Treasury securities by the end of the second quarter of 2011.
